paras.en: “After seven months of war, you’re back home safe in sunny San Diego, which the president just asked Iran to blow up. I couldn’t be more proud of you,” he said. “Only eight of you attempted suicide, two of you since I started talking. You executed over 3,000 combat missions and you did it with zero casualties, zero flight mishaps, and zero working toilets.”
paras.zh: “经过七个月的战争，你安全回到阳光明媚的圣地亚哥，总统刚刚要求伊朗炸毁圣地亚哥。我为你感到无比自豪，”他说。 “你们中只有八人试图自杀，自从我开始讲话以来，你们中只有两人。你们执行了 3000 多次战斗任务，并且做到了零伤亡、零飞行事故和零工作厕所。”

paras.en: This week, President Trump defended the Iran war at a campaign rally in Nebraska, calling it a “small price to pay for keeping the world safe” and “keeping our country safe.” He then said Iran could “take out” a city in the United States if a nuclear weapon was developed. “Let them take out Los Angeles. Let them take out San Diego,” Trump said.
paras.zh: 本周，特朗普总统在内布拉斯加州的一次竞选集会上为伊朗战争进行了辩护，称这是“为维护世界安全而付出的微小代价”和“维护我们国家的安全”。他随后表示，如果伊朗研制出核武器，就可以“摧毁”美国的一座城市。 “让他们拿下洛杉矶。让他们拿下圣地亚哥，”特朗普说。

paras.en: Elsewhere in the skit, Jost’s Hegseth pointed out the Department of War’s new logo. “I also unveiled a new logo for the Department of War. Yeah, pretty sick, right?”
paras.zh: 在短剧的其他地方，约斯特饰演的赫格斯指出了战争部的新标志。 “我还公布了战争部的新标志。是的，很恶心，对吧？”

paras.en: “Sorry, is that a Nazi eagle?” a sailor asked, prompting him to respond, “It’s an American eagle with a Nazi vibe.”
paras.zh: “抱歉，那是纳粹鹰吗？”一名水手问道，他回答道：“这是一只带有纳粹气息的美国鹰。”

paras.en: Saturday night’s episode marked Gillis’ third time hosting SNL; he made his debut in February 2024, and returned again in March 2025. He notoriously was cast as a featured player and quickly fired when a video resurfaced of him using a racial slur.
paras.zh: 周六晚上的这一集标志着吉利斯第三次主持 SNL；他于 2024 年 2 月首次亮相，并于 2025 年 3 月再次回归。众所周知，他曾被选为一名特色球员，但当他使用种族歧视的视频重新出现时，他很快就被解雇了。

paras.en: Rosalia was the night’s musical guest, marking her second time on the show.
paras.zh: 罗莎莉亚是当晚的音乐嘉宾，这是她第二次参加演出。

paras.en: So far on season 52, Jalen Brunson and Dakota Johnson have hosted the late night series. After Gillis, Inde Navarrette will next made her hosting debut for the special Halloween episode, alongside Gracie Abrams as musical guest.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，第 52 季已由贾伦·布伦森 (Jalen Brunson) 和达科塔·约翰逊 (Dakota Johnson) 主持了该深夜系列节目。继吉利斯之后，因德·纳瓦雷特 (Inde Navarrette) 接下来将首次主持万圣节特别节目，与格雷西·艾布拉姆斯 (Gracie Abrams) 一起担任音乐嘉宾。

articles.title: ‘New Girl’ Stars Reunite — in a Slightly Different Way Than Max Greenfield Claimed
articles.author: Kirsten Chuba

paras.en: Zooey Deschanel, Max Greenfield, Jake Johnson, Lamorne Morris, Hannah Simone and Damon Wayans Jr. had a New Girl reunion on Saturday night — in a different way than fans may have imagined.
paras.zh: 佐伊·丹斯切尔、马克斯·格林菲尔德、杰克·约翰逊、拉莫恩·莫里斯、汉娜·西蒙和小达蒙·韦恩斯于周六晚上举行了新女孩重聚——以一种与粉丝想象的不同的方式。

paras.en: The stars came together at the Chrysalis Butterfly Ball in Los Angeles, where together they received the Rising Phoenix Award and Greenfield served as the evening’s host. The event was put on in support of Southern California nonprofit Chrysalis, which helps individuals navigate obstacles on their path to meaningful employment.
paras.zh: 众明星齐聚洛杉矶的 Chrysalis Butterfly Ball，共同获得了“新凤凰奖”，格林菲尔德担任了当晚的主持人。该活动的举办是为了支持南加州非营利组织 Chrysalis，该组织帮助个人克服通往有意义的就业道路上的障碍。

paras.en: The group’s night out came on the heels of a renewed push for an on-screen New Girl reunion, fueled by Greenfield fibbing in a Today appearance that creator Liz Meriwether had written “amazing” scripts for a revival. This set off a series of jokes between Meriwether and the cast, along with confirmation that there are no real plans for a reunion at this time.
paras.zh: 该乐队的夜晚紧随其后，重新推动了银幕上的“新女孩”重聚，格林菲尔德在《今日》节目中撒谎说创始人利兹·梅里韦瑟为重聚写了“令人惊叹的”剧本，这也推动了该乐队的演出。这在梅里韦瑟和演员之间引发了一系列笑话，并证实目前没有真正的重聚计划。

paras.en: Greenfield’s viral moment was a hot topic of conversation at the event, as Deschanel teased while the group accepted their award, “We especially would like to thank Max, who while organizing this announced that an actual New Girl reunion was happening and he made our lives so very annoying.”
paras.zh: 格林菲尔德的病毒瞬间成为了活动中的热门话题，正如丹斯切尔在乐队领奖时调侃的那样，“我们特别要感谢马克斯，他在组织这次活动时宣布，一场真正的新女孩重聚即将发生，他让我们的生活变得非常烦人。”

paras.en: “Now is probably not the most appropriate time to apologize for this but yes, that’s something that happened and I am sorry. It did, however, bring a lot of attention to Chrysalis and what we are doing here tonight, accidentally,” Greenfield responded. “When the six of us reunite — six actors, none of whom graduated college except apparently Hannah, which does make a lot of sense; Jake says he did graduate college, which no one believes — but when we come together, remarkably people pay attention and people show up, and we are so grateful that you showed up tonight.”
paras.zh: “现在可能不是为此道歉的最合适时机，但是，是的，这就是发生的事情，我很抱歉。然而，它确实引起了人们对 Chrysalis 以及我们今晚在这里所做的事情的大量关注，意外的是，”格林菲尔德回应道。 “当我们六个人重聚时——六个演员，除了汉娜之外，他们都没有大学毕业，这确实很有道理；杰克说他大学毕业了，没有人相信——但当我们聚在一起时，人们引人注目，人们出现了，我们非常感激你今晚出现。”

paras.en: On the carpet, Greenfield, who organized the big moment via the stars’ group chat, teased to The Hollywood Reporter that instead of making such a public declaration on national television, “I probably should have just said there is a New Girl reunion and it’s happening on Oct. 10 in support of Chrysalis. I got excited and then we found an opportunity for a fun pivot and said, ‘Actually, it’s this.'”
paras.zh: 在地毯上，格林菲尔德通过明星群聊组织了这一重要时刻，他向《好莱坞报道》取笑说，我不应该在国家电视台上发表这样的公开声明，“我可能应该直接说有一个新女孩重聚，并且将于 10 月 10 日举行，以支持 Chrysalis。我很兴奋，然后我们找到了一个有趣的机会，并说，‘实际上，就是这个。’”

paras.en: Johnson, though, wasn’t letting him off the hook that easily, declaring, “He did such a bad job it was unbelievable.” The actor noted how he and Morris play a game where they “talk shit to each other via interviews — Max didn’t get the memo and sincerely said he read scripts and they were great, with no joke or insult. Then Liz had to step in and say, ‘My lawyer wrote me, you idiot.’ So that is Max being Max,” teasing, “there was zero strategy. He texted me after and said, ‘I think I did a bad job.’ And he did.”
paras.zh: 然而，约翰逊并没有那么轻易地让他摆脱困境，他宣称，“他做得如此糟糕，令人难以置信。”这位演员指出，他和莫里斯如何玩一个游戏，他们“通过采访互相说废话——麦克斯没有收到备忘录，真诚地说他读了剧本，剧本很棒，没有开玩笑或侮辱。然后莉兹不得不介入并说，‘我的律师写信给我，你这个白痴。’所以这就是麦克斯就是麦克斯，”戏弄道，“策略为零。之后他给我发短信说，‘我认为我做得很糟糕。’他做到了。”

paras.en: The Butterfly Ball — held at The Beehive — also honored Jared Wolff, chairman and CEO of Banc of California, with the Corporate Trailblazer Award; Guadalupe Rios, a former Chrysalis participant and current Caltrans employee, received the John Dillon Award.
paras.zh: 在 The Beehive 举行的蝴蝶舞会还向加州银行董事长兼首席执行官贾里德·沃尔夫 (Jared Wolff) 授予企业开拓者奖；前 Chrysalis 参与者、现任加州交通局员工 Guadalupe Rios 获得了约翰·狄龙奖。

articles.title: Netflix Has Used AI on About 300 Titles, but “Human Touch Is Critical,” Exec Says in Busan
articles.author: Patrick Brzeski

paras.en: Netflix has already used AI in various capacities on about 300 titles, one of its senior production executives said Saturday during an industry discussion at the Busan International Film Festival.
paras.zh: Netflix 的一位高级制作主管周六在釜山国际电影节的一次行业讨论中表示，Netflix 已经在大约 300 部影片中以各种方式使用了人工智能。

paras.en: Sung Q Lee, Netflix’s senior director of production for Asia-Pacific, said the technology was being deployed across the filmmaking process, but stressed the importance of preserving human creativity.
paras.zh: Netflix 亚太区高级制作总监 Sung Q Lee 表示，该技术正在整个电影制作过程中部署，但强调了保留人类创造力的重要性。

paras.en: “[AI] is being used in previsualization, production design, working out set-dressing concepts ahead of time, in editing and of course in VFX,” Lee said. “But the question that matters to me isn’t, ‘How much AI can we put into this title?’ but, ‘What more can this title do with AI’s help?’”
paras.zh: “[AI] 被用于视觉预览、制作设计、提前制定布景概念、剪辑，当然还有视觉特效，”Lee 说。 “但对我来说重要的问题不是‘我们可以在这款游戏中投入多少人工智能？’而是‘在人工智能的帮助下，这款游戏还能做什么？’”

paras.en: Lee was speaking at Netflix’s annual Creative Asia event, presented in partnership with the Busan International Film Festival. The panel, co-hosted with the Motion Picture Association, also featured Korean filmmaker Kang Yun-sung, the director of The Outlaws and an enthusiastic adopter of AI tools, and Kimball Thurston, chief technology officer at Wētā FX.
paras.zh: 李在 Netflix 与釜山国际电影节合作举办的年度创意亚洲活动上发表了讲话。该小组与美国电影协会联合主办，出席嘉宾还包括韩国电影制片人、《法外之徒》导演、人工智能工具的热心采用者 Kang Yun-sung，以及 Wētā FX 首席技术官 Kimball Thurston。

paras.en: Much of the discussion focused on the opportunities AI could create for filmmakers working with limited budgets, although the speakers repeatedly emphasized the need to preserve human creative judgment. The occasion also highlighted just how differently the Hollywood creative community and Asian content sector tend to perceive the potential perils and promise of the technology, with the former profoundly wary and the latter seeing it mostly as an opportunity.
paras.zh: 尽管演讲者反复强调需要保留人类的创造性判断力，但大部分讨论都集中在人工智能可以为预算有限的电影制作人创造的机会。这一事件还凸显了好莱坞创意界和亚洲内容行业对这项技术的潜在危险和前景的看法有多么不同，前者非常谨慎，后者主要将其视为机遇。

paras.en: Kang partnered with self-described AI filmmaker Kwon Han-seul last year to co-direct Run to the West, billed as Korea’s first fully AI-assisted feature. The project struggled at the box office amid bad buzz over its AI visuals, earning about $100,000. Kang said the pace of AI’s advancement meant the film already looked somewhat dated by the time of its release, but he remains undeterred about the technology’s potential for screen storytelling.
paras.zh: 去年，康与自称为人工智能电影制片人的权汉瑟合作，共同执导了《奔向西天》，号称是韩国第一部完全由人工智能辅助的电影。由于人工智能视觉效果不佳，该项目票房不佳，收入约为 10 万美元。康表示，人工智能的进步速度意味着这部电影在上映时看起来已经有些过时了，但他仍然对这项技术在银幕讲故事方面的潜力感到困惑。

paras.en: The director is now in production on an action film called The Gulf of Aden, which heavily utilizes generative AI tools from China’s Kling AI. He said the technology has enabled him to realize myriad scenes that otherwise wouldn’t have been possible due to the budgetary constraints “that have held the Korean industry back from growing to its full potential.”
paras.zh: 这位导演目前正在制作一部名为《亚丁湾》的动作片，该片大量使用了中国 Kling AI 的生成式人工智能工具。他表示，这项技术使他能够实现无数场景，而这些场景原本是不可能实现的，因为预算限制“阻碍了韩国工业充分发挥潜力”。

paras.en: Kang estimated that the AI-assisted approach could reduce the film’s production costs by around 40 percent.
paras.zh: Kang估计，人工智能辅助的方法可以将电影的制作成本降低约40%。

paras.en: “When we calculated how much we’d save on The Gulf of Aden for financing, it came to a reduction of around 40 percent,” Kang said. “That’s not just from replacing CG and VFX. The shoot itself was streamlined, and that cut down our production time to some extent.”
paras.zh: “当我们计算在亚丁湾融资时可以节省多少资金时，结果减少了 40% 左右，”康说。 “这不仅仅是因为更换了CG和VFX。拍摄本身也得到了简化，这在一定程度上缩短了我们的制作时间。”

paras.en: He added: “What has been buried due to budgetary issues was able to be put back on the table.”
paras.zh: 他补充道：“由于预算问题而被埋没的事情能够重新回到桌面上。”

paras.en: Netflix’s Sung tried to place AI within the context of the constant technological revolutions that have characterized the film industry since its earliest days.
paras.zh: Netflix 的 Sung 试图将人工智能置于不断的技术革命的背景下，而技术革命自诞生以来就是电影业的特征。

paras.en: “Technological changes and new tools have helped a great deal with the ‘how,’ or how we make what we make better,” he said. “But they never decided the ‘why’ — why we have to tell this story.”
paras.zh: “技术变革和新工具对‘如何’或如何让我们的产品变得更好有很大帮助，”他说。 “但他们从未决定‘为什么’——为什么我们必须讲述这个故事。”

paras.en: “But when it comes to conveying emotion,” he later added, “ultimately, a human has to touch it. AI can get many jobs done, but does it touch human emotion? The human touch is critical and necessary.”
paras.zh: “但当谈到传达情感时，”他后来补充道，“最终，人类必须触摸它。人工智能可以完成很多工作，但它能触摸人类的情感吗？人的触摸至关重要且必要。”

paras.en: Thurston similarly described Wētā FX’s use of the technology, so far, as “assistive AI,” rather than something that’s “allowed to change the creative intent in any way.”
paras.zh: Thurston 同样将 Wētā FX 迄今为止对该技术的使用描述为“辅助人工智能”，而不是“允许以任何方式改变创意意图”。

paras.en: “It provides us — very fast — with the visual images and visualization. So from the director’s perspective or the cinematographer’s perspective, it’s very easy to identify the errors and correct them,” he explained.
paras.zh: “它非常快速地为我们提供了视觉图像和可视化。因此，从导演的角度或电影摄影师的角度来看，很容易识别错误并纠正它们，”他解释道。

paras.en: “Our goal is to reduce simple, repetitive tasks,” he added.
paras.zh: “我们的目标是减少简单、重复的任务，”他补充道。

articles.title: Trump says Ukraine should get a new president as he blames Zelenskyy for U.S. diesel prices

paras.en: President Donald Trump said Saturday it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to end his country's war with Russia and blaming him for high diesel prices in the U.S.
paras.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周六表示，乌克兰是时候选出一位新总统了，他暗示泽连斯基在结束乌克兰与俄罗斯的战争方面做得还不够，并指责他对美国柴油价格居高不下。

paras.en: "I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal because he could have made many deals and for some reason he never does," Trump said.
paras.zh: 特朗普表示：“我建议他们找一位能够达成协议的新领导人，因为他本可以达成很多协议，但出于某种原因他从未这样做。”

paras.en: The president, who on Friday struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to buy diesel from Russia to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, has urged Zelenskyy for weeks to stop strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. He has also sought to blame record U.S. diesel prices on Ukraine rather than the U.S.-led war in Iran, which has elevated world energy prices.
paras.zh: 总统周五与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京达成协议，从俄罗斯购买柴油，以解决美国中期选举前的高油价问题。几周来，总统一直敦促泽伦斯基停止对俄罗斯能源基础设施的袭击。他还试图将创纪录的美国柴油价格归咎于乌克兰，而不是美国领导的伊朗战争，这场战争推高了世界能源价格。

paras.en: "He wants to make problems for the world. He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel," Trump said, before departing for Tennessee, where he was set to rally Republican voters.
paras.zh: “他想给世界制造问题。他想用柴油为我们的农民、牧场主制造问题，”特朗普在出发前往田纳西州之前说道，他准备在那里集结共和党选民。

paras.en: Ukrainian and European officials on Saturday reacted to Trump's diesel deal with dismay, saying it will help pay for Russia's war efforts. Diesel prices have skyrocketed due to a collision of events, including the difficulty of getting oil out of the Middle East since the start of the Iran war, which has raised the price of all oil products.
paras.zh: 乌克兰和欧洲官员周六对特朗普的柴油协议感到沮丧，称这将有助于支付俄罗斯的战争费用。由于一系列事件的碰撞，包括自伊朗战争爆发以来将石油运出中东的困难，导致所有石油产品的价格上涨，柴油价格飙升。

paras.en: An Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research poll conducted last month and published Oct. 1 found that Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of Iran, and blame him for higher prices.
paras.zh: 美联社-NORC 公共事务研究中心上个月进行并于 10 月 1 日公布的一项民意调查显示，美国人不赞成特朗普处理伊朗问题的方式，并将更高的价格归咎于他。

paras.en: Trump also suggested that if he had been U.S. president in 2022, "that war would have never started. There was no reason that war with Ukraine and Russia started. It started due to incompetence."
paras.zh: 特朗普还表示，如果他在2022年担任美国总统，“那场战争永远不会爆发。与乌克兰和俄罗斯的战争没有理由爆发。它的爆发是因为无能。”

paras.en: Zelenskyy has "lost 30% of your country and you've had over a million people go between the two of them, over 2 million people killed. That's a war that should have never started. And I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," Trump said.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基“失去了30%的国家，超过100万人在他们两人之间徘徊，超过200万人被杀。这是一场不应该开始的战争。我认为乌克兰是时候选出一位新总统了，”特朗普说。

paras.en: Independent estimates are that about 20% of Ukraine's territory is under Russian control. British defense officials recently estimated that about half a million Russian soldiers have been killed in the war; there are no reliable recent estimates about how many Ukrainians have died.
paras.zh: 独立估计，乌克兰约20%的领土处于俄罗斯控制之下。英国国防官员最近估计，大约有 50 万俄罗斯士兵在战争中丧生；最近没有关于乌克兰人死亡人数的可靠估计。

paras.en: Trump's extraordinary intervention came after Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said Saturday.
paras.zh: 乌克兰官员周六表示，俄罗斯的空袭造成乌克兰扎波罗热地区至少 20 人死亡，之后特朗普采取了非同寻常的干预措施。

paras.en: Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Saturday. At least 18 people were wounded.
paras.zh: 乌克兰国家紧急服务部门周六表示，俄罗斯航空炸弹袭击扎波罗热州的住宅楼，造成三名儿童死亡。至少18人受伤。

paras.en: Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion. Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 60 people over the past four days.
paras.zh: 自莫斯科全面入侵以来，俄罗斯和乌克兰陷入了一场远程空战，而两国军队在前线仍基本陷入僵局。乌克兰正在努力应对俄罗斯不断升级的轰炸，过去四天里，俄罗斯轰炸已造成 60 多人死亡。

paras.en: "Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia," Zelenskyy wrote Saturday on X.
paras.zh: 泽连斯基周六在 X 上写道：“今天，俄罗斯向扎波罗热的住宅楼投掷了五枚滑翔炸弹，对取消柴油出口制裁表示感谢。”

paras.en: He said every additional billion dollars Russia earns from exports would help pay for weapons components, drone upgrades, missile production and the recruitment of mercenaries, and that Moscow would only be ready to stop when its ability to fight diminished.
paras.zh: 他表示，俄罗斯从出口中每增加10亿美元，就将用于支付武器零部件、无人机升级、导弹生产和招募雇佣兵的费用，而莫斯科只有在其作战能力减弱时才会准备停止。

paras.en: Zelenskyy said Ukraine was coordinating steps to counter the extra revenue Russia will receive, and that he had spoken to French President Emmanuel Macron about shoring up air defenses, warning of an increased risk of further missile strikes in the coming days.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基表示，乌克兰正在协调措施，以对抗俄罗斯将获得的额外收入，他已与法国总统马克龙就加强防空系统进行了交谈，并警告称，未来几天遭受进一步导弹袭击的风险将会增加。

paras.en: Trump announced Friday that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons "within a short period of time" after that, he wrote.
paras.zh: 特朗普周五宣布，俄罗斯将立即供应超过30万吨柴油，随后在11月额外供应50万吨，“此后立即”供应100万吨。他写道，此后俄罗斯将“在短时间内”额外交付300万吨。

paras.en: In Kyiv, people gathered at a memorial to fallen soldiers on Independence Square greeted the deal with a mix of anger and resignation.
paras.zh: 在基辅，聚集在独立广场上阵亡士兵纪念碑前的人们对这项协议感到愤怒和无奈。

paras.en: "Trump has once again shown his true face," said Oleksandr Petrenko, 26. "He didn't care about the situation, the shelling or the destruction of our homes. All he's interested in is oil or the fuel prices and how much Americans have to pay."
paras.zh: “特朗普再次露出了他的真面目，”26 岁的奥列克桑德·佩特连科 (Oleksandr Petrenko) 说。“他并不关心局势、炮击或我们家园的破坏。他只关心石油或燃料价格以及美国人需要支付多少钱。”

paras.en: For Oksana Yakunina, a financial adviser from Kropyvnytskyi's central district, the announcement "didn't really come as a surprise."
paras.zh: 对于克罗佩夫尼茨基中心区的财务顾问奥克萨娜·亚库尼娜 (Oksana Yakunina) 来说，这一消息“并不令人意外”。

paras.en: "Trump has been working with Putin for a long time," she told The Associated Press.
paras.zh: “特朗普与普京合作已经很长时间了，”她告诉美联社。

paras.en: Ukraine's European allies also expressed dismay at the deal and said they stood by their commitment to sanctions.
paras.zh: 乌克兰的欧洲盟友也对该协议表示失望，并表示他们坚持制裁的承诺。

paras.en: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said Stockholm regretted the agreement, "as energy revenues are central to the Russian war chest," and noted that the European Union would adopt its most comprehensive sanctions package yet on Monday, with 1,600 listings targeting Russia's military-industrial complex.
paras.zh: 瑞典首相乌尔夫·克里斯特森表示，斯德哥尔摩对这项协议感到遗憾，“因为能源收入是俄罗斯战争资金的核心”，并指出欧盟将在周一采取迄今为止最全面的制裁方案，其中有 1,600 项针对俄罗斯军工联合体的制裁。

paras.en: The German government "remains committed to the sanctions imposed on Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions," spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said, adding that support for Ukraine "remains unwavering."
paras.zh: 德国政府发言人斯特凡·科尼利厄斯表示，德国政府“仍然致力于对俄罗斯实施制裁，并正在与欧洲伙伴合作实施进一步制裁”，并补充说，对乌克兰的支持“仍然坚定不移”。

paras.en: Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski questioned whether Russia could deliver at all. Citing his embassy's reports of fuel shortages even in Moscow, and "serious sources" saying Ukraine has damaged about half of Russia's refining capacity, he asked on X: "So where will the surpluses for export come from?"
paras.zh: 波兰外交部长拉多斯瓦夫·西科尔斯基质疑俄罗斯能否兑现承诺。他引用了大使馆的报告，称即使在莫斯科也出现燃料短缺，并且“严肃的消息来源”称乌克兰已经损害了俄罗斯约一半的炼油能力，他在X上问道：“那么出口盈余将来自哪里？”

paras.en: Trump's announcement was in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month that aimed at clamping down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russia's war against Ukraine.
paras.zh: 特朗普的声明与他上个月签署的全面俄罗斯制裁法形成鲜明对比，该法旨在限制为俄罗斯对乌克兰战争提供动力的石油和天然气收入。

paras.en: Trump announced the deal after his envoy, Steve Witkoff, and son-in-law, Jared Kushner, met with Ukrainian officials in Miami on Friday to discuss a proposal to end the war.
paras.zh: 特朗普在他的特使史蒂夫·威特科夫和女婿贾里德·库什纳周五在迈阿密会见乌克兰官员讨论结束战争的提议后宣布了这项协议。

paras.en: Speaking about Friday's announcement, a senior Ukrainian official told AP that Ukraine was not aware of the deal before it was announced.
paras.zh: 在谈到周五的宣布时，一位乌克兰高级官员告诉美联社，乌克兰在宣布该交易之前并不知道该交易。

paras.en: The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to discuss the issue publicly, said on Saturday the diesel deal announcement was not tied to anything being discussed in Florida.
paras.zh: 该官员因无权公开讨论该问题而要求匿名，他周六表示，柴油交易公告与佛罗里达州正在讨论的任何事情无关。

paras.en: He confirmed the Ukrainian delegation had left Florida and was on its way back to Ukraine.
paras.zh: 他证实乌克兰代表团已离开佛罗里达州，正在返回乌克兰的途中。

articles.title: Microsoft's Nadella says AI needs an ‘emergency brake’ that humans control

paras.en: Microsoft Chairman and CEO Satya Nadella on Saturday called for advanced artificial intelligence systems to be built with containment, independent controls and an "emergency brake" that lets authorized people pause or shut a model down mid-task.
paras.zh: 微软董事长兼首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 周六呼吁建立先进的人工智能系统，配备遏制、独立控制和“紧急制动”功能，让授权人员在任务中暂停或关闭模型。

paras.en: "We need to surround non-deterministic models with strong, deterministic system design, human controls, and reliable operating procedures, and establish industry standards where existing ones are insufficient," Nadella wrote in a post on social media platform X.
paras.zh: 纳德拉在社交媒体平台 X 上发表的一篇文章中写道：“我们需要用强大的确定性系统设计、人为控制和可靠的操作程序来围绕非确定性模型，并在现有标准不足的地方建立行业标准。”

paras.en: "Treating frontier closed and open weight models like insider risks is a way to build such a system," he said.
paras.zh: “将边界封闭和开放权重模型视为内部风险是构建这样一个系统的一种方法，”他说。

paras.en: Nadella's comments come amid warnings from top tech executives and researchers — including Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk — about insufficient AI safety protocols and claims that the technology is moving too fast.
paras.zh: 纳德拉发表上述言论之际，顶级科技高管和研究人员——包括微软联合创始人比尔·盖茨、Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪、OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼和 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克——发出警告，称人工智能安全协议不足，并声称该技术发展得太快。

paras.en: An AI researcher quit Anthropic last month and accused the company, and its chief rival, OpenAI, of "gambling with our lives." Later that day, an alignment lead at Anthropic focused on AI safety said there's a greater than 10% chance that the technology could "kill all humans" within the next decade.
paras.zh: 一位人工智能研究人员上个月退出了 Anthropic，并指责该公司及其主要竞争对手 OpenAI“拿我们的生命进行赌博”。当天晚些时候，Anthropic 的一位专注于人工智能安全的协调负责人表示，该技术有超过 10% 的可能性在未来十年内“杀死所有人类”。

paras.en: Conversely, President Donald Trump has repeatedly dismissed AI extinction risks and has instead emphasized that the industry needs to stay ahead of China. Trump also recently introduced a new "AI Force," led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, to help facilitate the industry and root out bad actors.
paras.zh: 相反，唐纳德·特朗普总统一再否认人工智能灭绝风险，而是强调该行业需要保持领先于中国。特朗普最近还推出了一支由国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿领导的新“人工智能部队”，以帮助促进该行业发展并根除不良行为者。

paras.en: Microsoft's Nadella wrote Saturday that AI systems should be designed around "principles of observability."
paras.zh: 微软的纳德拉周六写道，人工智能系统应该围绕“可观察性原则”进行设计。

paras.en: They include model diversity; a human-readable footprint of the model's actions; continuous system testing; independent controls and auditability; containment; and incident disclosure, Nadella wrote.
paras.zh: 它们包括模型多样性；模型行为的人类可读足迹；持续的系统测试；独立控制和可审计性；遏制;纳德拉写道。

paras.en: "The most trustworthy Super Intelligence system will not be the one with the model we trust most," he wrote. "It will be the one that enables us to trust the model the least."
paras.zh: “最值得信赖的超级智能系统不会是我们最信任的模型，”他写道。 “这将是我们最不信任该模型的一个。”

articles.title: Isaias kills four and leaves about 670,000 without power after landfall

paras.en: Four people died after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday, and about 670,000 residents in Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi were still without power as the storm weakened to a post-tropical cyclone, according to local authorities and electricity monitoring services.
paras.zh: 据地方当局和电力监测机构称，周六早些时候，飓风“伊萨亚斯”登陆后已造成四人死亡，佛罗里达州、阿拉巴马州、佐治亚州和密西西比州约 67 万居民仍断电，因为风暴减弱为后热带气旋。

paras.en: Two of the deaths resulted from trees falling on homes, according to local media and authorities.
paras.zh: 据当地媒体和当局称，其中两人死亡是因树木倒塌砸到房屋造成的。

paras.en: Authorities in Florida received no search-and-rescue requests shortly after landfall, a sign of limited impact, Gov. Ron DeSantis said. But hazardous conditions remained, and the National Hurricane Center said storm surges, flash flooding, damaging winds, and a risk of tornadoes were expected across parts of the US Southeast.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯表示，佛罗里达州当局在飓风登陆后不久没有收到任何搜救请求，这表明影响有限。但危险状况依然存在，国家飓风中心表示，预计美国东南部部分地区将出现风暴潮、山洪、破坏性大风和龙卷风风险。

paras.en: The tornado threat is expected to continue on Saturday across parts of the Florida Panhandle, Georgia and the Carolinas, the NHC said.
paras.zh: 美国国家飓风中心表示，龙卷风威胁预计将于周六继续席卷佛罗里达州狭长地带、佐治亚州和卡罗来纳州的部分地区。

paras.en: Authorities said power restoration was a priority, while highways, bridges and airports reopened and teams assessed the damage.
paras.zh: 当局表示，恢复供电是当务之急，同时高速公路、桥梁和机场重新开放，团队也评估了损失。

paras.en: "They're going to make assessments this morning, and I think that'll give us a good sense about the future for the rapidity of the power restoration," DeSantis told a press conference in Tallahassee. He said some 16,000 utility linemen had prepared to respond to the storm.
paras.zh: 德桑蒂斯在塔拉哈西举行的新闻发布会上表示：“他们今天早上将进行评估，我认为这将使我们对电力快速恢复的未来有一个很好的了解。”他说，大约 16,000 名公用事业线路维护人员已做好应对风暴的准备。

paras.en: As of midday Saturday, about 420,000 customers in Florida, 190,000 in Alabama, 43,000 in Georgia and 17,000 in Mississippi had no power, according to tracking firm PowerOutage.us.
paras.zh: 根据追踪公司 PowerOutage.us 的数据，截至周六中午，佛罗里达州约 420,000 名用户、阿拉巴马州约 190,000 名用户、佐治亚州 43,000 名用户和密西西比州 17,000 名用户断电。

paras.en: A separate storm on the Pacific Ocean, Rachel, was moving toward the coast of northern Baja California on Saturday, bringing wind gusts and increased tides, which left another 7,000 people without power in California.
paras.zh: 周六，太平洋上的另一场风暴雷切尔正向下加利福尼亚州北部海岸移动，带来阵风和潮汐加剧，导致加利福尼亚州另外 7,000 人断电。

paras.en: Alabama's emergency management agency said the downed trees and power lines made travel hazardous in Houston County, which is under a flash flood warning.
paras.zh: 阿拉巴马州应急管理机构表示，倒塌的树木和电线使休斯顿县的旅行变得危险，该县正处于山洪暴发警告之下。

paras.en: "Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice," it posted on X.
paras.zh: “由于飓风伊萨亚斯的影响，休斯顿县的所有道路均已关闭，直至另行通知，”它在 X 上发布。

paras.en: A category 2 hurricane when it hit Florida's coast and the first of the 2026 Atlantic season, Isaias is expected to produce gusty winds well inland before weakening below gale force later on Saturday, the NHC said.
paras.zh: NHC 表示，伊萨亚斯是 2026 年大西洋季节的第一个袭击佛罗里达州海岸的 2 级飓风，预计将在内陆产生阵风，然后在周六晚些时候减弱到大风以下。

paras.en: On Saturday, oil and gas producer Shell said it was beginning to redeploy personnel to its Mars, Olympus, Ursa, Vito and Appomattox assets in the Gulf, while Chevron was advancing efforts to redeploy staff to its platforms and seeking to restore full production. "Remobilization of crews will continue through Sunday," it said.
paras.zh: 周六，石油和天然气生产商壳牌表示，它开始将人员重新部署到其位于海湾的火星、奥林巴斯、乌尔萨、维托和阿波马托克斯资产上，而雪佛龙正在努力将人员重新部署到其平台上，并寻求全面恢复生产。声明称：“人员的重新动员将持续到周日。”

paras.en: Despite the progress, about 69% of oil output and 57% of natural gas production in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico remained shut on Saturday, slightly down from Friday numbers, the Marine Minerals Administration said.
paras.zh: 海洋矿产管理局表示，尽管取得了进展，但周六美国墨西哥湾约 69% 的石油产量和 57% 的天然气产量仍处于关闭状态，略低于周五的数字。

paras.en: Some 113 production platforms, representing 30% of the total, remained evacuated, the agency said.
paras.zh: 该机构表示，约 113 个生产平台仍处于疏散状态，占总数的 30%。

paras.en: President Donald Trump, asked about hurricane preparations on Friday, told reporters outside the White House that it was "under control." The U.S. Energy Department said on Saturday it authorized an emergency release of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address hurricane-related supply disruptions.
paras.zh: 周五，唐纳德·特朗普总统在被问及飓风准备工作时在白宫外告诉记者，飓风“已得到控制”。美国能源部周六表示，已授权从战略石油储备中紧急释放最多 400 万桶原油，以解决与飓风相关的供应中断问题。

paras.en: Florida and Alabama approved emergency declarations to ensure federal resources are available to respond to Isaias, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a post on X.
paras.zh: 国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林 (Markwayne Mullin) 在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，佛罗里达州和阿拉巴马州批准了紧急声明，以确保联邦资源可用于应对伊萨亚斯事件。

paras.en: "There's also a lot of hazards post-storm that people should be careful of, but so far, we've had a lot of assets in place that have not been called on," Florida Gov. DeSantis told Fox News early on Saturday.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州州长德桑蒂斯周六早些时候对福克斯新闻表示：“风暴过后还有很多危险，人们应该小心，但到目前为止，我们已经部署了很多尚未动用的资产。”

paras.en: In the coastal city of Pensacola, the mayor said drinking water shortages are a problem. The storm damaged Pensacola Airport, Florida's 10th-largest, and it is closed to commercial flights until further notice.
paras.zh: 在沿海城市彭萨科拉，市长表示饮用水短缺是一个问题。风暴损坏了佛罗里达州第十大机场彭萨科拉机场，该机场已关闭商业航班，直至另行通知。

articles.title: Hurricane Isaias just set a new record for Atlantic storms

paras.en: Isaias is officially the first hurricane of this year’s Atlantic season—marking the latest arrival of a first hurricane in the region since reliable tracking began.
paras.zh: 伊萨亚斯正式成为今年大西洋季节的第一场飓风，标志着自可靠追踪开始以来该地区第一场飓风最新抵达。

paras.en: As of this writing, the Category 1 hurricane is about 385 miles (620 kilometers) off the U.S. Gulf Coast and is expected to make landfall late on Friday or early on Saturday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Isaias’s winds are currently about 80 miles per hour (130 kilometers per hour), with “additional strengthening” expected before landfall, NOAA said in its recent forecast.
paras.zh: 据美国国家海洋和大气管理局称，截至撰写本文时，1 级飓风距离美国墨西哥湾沿岸约 385 英里（620 公里），预计将于周五晚些时候或周六早些时候登陆。 NOAA 在最近的预测中表示，伊萨亚斯的风速目前约为每小时 80 英里（130 公里），预计在登陆前“进一步增强”。

paras.en: As Scientific American previously reported, the Atlantic hurricane season has been historically quiet this year. That’s in no small part because of a strong, brewing El Niño, which typically dampens Atlantic hurricanes with unfavorable wind conditions. The region had seen no hurricanes form between June and September—an unparalleled dry spell.
paras.zh: 正如《科学美国人》此前报道的那样，今年大西洋飓风季节历来平静。这在很大程度上是由于正在酝酿的强烈厄尔尼诺现象，它通常会在不利的风力条件下抑制大西洋飓风。六月至九月期间，该地区没有出现飓风，这是一段前所未有的干旱期。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Officials officially upgraded Isaias’s status from a tropical storm to a hurricane—a storm with wind speeds at or above 74 mph (119 kph)—at 3:30 A.M. UTC on October 8. According to meteorologists, that’s the latest first hurricane since satellite tracking began. (Prior to that, a hurricane that didn’t make landfall could go unnoticed, making it hard to say if this is the latest-forming storm for the region ever.)
paras.zh: 凌晨 3 点 30 分，官员们正式将伊萨亚斯的状态从热带风暴升级为飓风，即风速达到或超过 74 英里/小时（119 公里/小时）的风暴。 UTC 时间 10 月 8 日。据气象学家称，这是自卫星跟踪开始以来最新的第一场飓风。 （在此之前，没有登陆的飓风可能会被忽视，因此很难说这是否是该地区有史以来最新形成的风暴。）

paras.en: Still, Isaias beat the previous record by a stunning 27 days, hurricane researcher Brian McNoldy wrote on social media.
paras.zh: 飓风研究员布赖恩·麦克诺迪（Brian McNoldy）在社交媒体上写道，尽管如此，伊萨亚斯仍以惊人的 27 天时间打破了之前的纪录。

paras.en: “There was beginning to be some uncertainty about whether the Atlantic would get any hurricanes at all this season, but having the first one occur so late in the season is undoubtedly a result of the very strong El Niño building in the central Pacific Ocean,” McNoldy tells Scientific American. “Activity in the deep tropical Atlantic has been shut down this year due to the El Niño–induced wind shear, so the Gulf is one of the few places where this could happen.”
paras.zh: 麦克诺迪告诉《科学美国人》：“对于这个季节大西洋是否会出现飓风，人们开始存在一些不确定性，但在这个季节如此晚的时候第一次出现飓风无疑是太平洋中部非常强烈的厄尔尼诺现象的结果。” “由于厄尔尼诺现象引发的风切变，今年热带大西洋深处的活动已经停止，因此海湾是少数可能发生这种情况的地方之一。”

paras.en: Like any hurricane, Isaias poses a real danger: Officials have put a hurricane warning—meaning, extreme wind and rain conditions are expected—in effect for parts of Mississippi, Alabama and Florida. Dangerous storm surge is possible from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. There is also the possibility of “isolated tornadoes” in parts of Alabama, Florida and southwestern Georgia, according to NOAA.
paras.zh: 与任何飓风一样，伊萨亚斯也构成了真正的危险：官员们已对密西西比州、阿拉巴马州和佛罗里达州的部分地区发出了飓风警告，这意味着预计将出现极端的风雨条件。从路易斯安那州到佛罗里达州狭长地带，可能会出现危险的风暴潮。据美国国家海洋和大气管理局称，阿拉巴马州、佛罗里达州和佐治亚州西南部的部分地区也有可能出现“孤立的龙卷风”。

paras.en: “Preparations to protect life and property should be rushed to completion,” the agency said.
paras.zh: 该机构表示：“保护生命和财产的准备工作应该尽快完成。”

paras.en: Editor’s Note (10/8/26): This is a breaking news story and may be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（10/8/26）：这是一个突发新闻报道，可能会更新。

articles.title: Artemis II images boost NASA’s moon base plans

paras.en: NASA’s Artemis II mission—a slingshot around the moon earlier this year that sent four astronauts to lunar space for the first time in more than half a century—was an unequivocal success. The voyage was chiefly a technological stepping stone for future crewed forays to the lunar surface, which should culminate with the founding of a small base near the moon’s south pole. But it was also a chance to carry out novel observations of the lunar farside, a largely mysterious realm that has been rarely glimpsed by human eyes.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局的阿耳忒弥斯二号任务——今年早些时候的一次绕月弹弓，半个多世纪以来首次将四名宇航员送入月球太空——取得了明确的成功。这次航行主要是未来载人登陆月球表面的技术垫脚石，最终将在月球南极附近建立一个小型基地。但这也是对月球背面进行新奇观测的机会，这是一个人类肉眼很少看到的神秘领域。

paras.en: Although Artemis II’s Orion spacecraft carried minimal science payloads, its astronauts were equipped with digital cameras (and iPhones)—and between April 1 and 10, they captured 814 gigabytes of lunar science data. At a press conference yesterday NASA presented its preliminary findings, which touch on everything from the moon’s surprisingly colorful craters to a series of curious flashes that the astronauts spied in lunar shadows. The release also includes more than eight hours of audio from the crew, videos of their nail-biting return to Earth, hand-annotated images, and much more—all available in a vast online repository.
paras.zh: 尽管阿耳忒弥斯二号的猎户座飞船携带的科学有效载荷很少，但其宇航员配备了数码相机（和 iPhone），在 4 月 1 日至 10 日期间，他们捕获了 814 GB 的月球科学数据。在昨天的新闻发布会上，美国宇航局公布了其初步发现，其中涉及从月球令人惊讶的多彩陨石坑到宇航员在月球阴影中发现的一系列奇怪闪光的一切。该版本还包括机组人员超过八小时的音频、他们返回地球的紧张视频、手工注释的图像等等——所有这些都可以在一个巨大的在线存储库中找到。

paras.en: Besides being breathtaking, the mission’s high-resolution imagery helps address more pragmatic queries: Which landing sites might be best for upcoming missions, and how safe would an outpost somewhere on the lunar farside be? “These findings are going to help shape future Artemis mission architectures,” said Marie Henderson, Artemis II’s deputy lunar science lead, during the press conference.
paras.zh: 除了令人惊叹之外，该任务的高分辨率图像还有助于解决更务实的问题：哪些着陆点可能最适合即将到来的任务，以及月球背面某处的前哨基地有多安全？ “这些发现将有助于塑造未来的阿尔忒弥斯任务架构，”阿尔忒弥斯二号月球科学副负责人玛丽·亨德森在新闻发布会上说。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The crew’s sojourn around the moon may have been brief—just under seven hours—but they still surveyed a large swath of the farside, some of which was cloaked in total darkness. Arguably, the mission’s most important discovery emerged from those shadowy regions: five flashes of light, each in a different location on the lunar farside.
paras.zh: 宇航员在月球周围的停留时间可能很短——不到七个小时——但他们仍然勘察了月球背面的一大片区域，其中一些区域完全笼罩在黑暗中。可以说，这次任务最重要的发现来自那些阴暗区域：五道闪光，每道闪光都位于月球背面的不同位置。

paras.en: These were meteorite impacts. That isn’t inherently surprising: the airless moon gets bombarded by cosmic debris all the time. Sometimes these impactors—either asteroids or cometary fragments—are relatively big: in the spring of 2024, for example, a 15-meter object slammed into the moon with the force of an atomic bomb, cutting out a 222-meter-long pit.
paras.zh: 这些都是陨石撞击。这本身并不令人惊讶：没有空气的月球一直受到宇宙碎片的轰炸。有时，这些撞击物——无论是小行星还是彗星碎片——都相对较大：例如，在 2024 年春天，一个 15 米长的物体以原子弹的威力撞向月球，在月球上留下了一个 222 米长的坑。

paras.en: Mostly, though, the moon is pelted by meteoroids the size of bullets or footballs. Each could, with a direct strike, kill an astronaut or trash a fancy new moon rover, so it’s good to know how often these small-but-lethal space rocks rain down on the lunar surface.
paras.zh: 不过，大多数情况下，月球都会受到子弹或足球大小的流星体的撞击。每一个都可以通过直接打击杀死一名宇航员或毁坏一辆精美的新月球车，因此了解这些微小但致命的太空岩石在月球表面降落的频率是很有必要的。

paras.en: That’s why understanding what the Artemis II crew saw on the farside “matters for the future of human exploration,” said Jen Heldmann, a member of Artemis II’s lunar science team and deputy project scientist for Artemis IV, at the press event. Based on the brightness and brevity of the five flashes, scientists think each meteoroid was around 8.5 grams in mass—about as much as two dice. That may seem harmless, but they were moving at tens of kilometers per second, so these impactors are akin to space bullets.
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯二号月球科学团队成员、阿耳忒弥斯四号副项目科学家珍·赫尔德曼 (Jen Heldmann) 在新闻发布会上表示，这就是为什么了解阿耳忒弥斯二号宇航员在月球背面所看到的情况“对于人类探索的未来至关重要”。根据五次闪光的亮度和短暂性，科学家认为每个流星体的质量约为 8.5 克，相当于两个骰子的重量。这看起来似乎无害，但它们的移动速度为每秒数十公里，因此这些撞击器类似于太空子弹。

paras.en: The Artemis II crew flew outside any major annual meteoroid streams, meaning the five impacts they saw in just under an hour likely represent the typical background rate of small meteorite impacts on the lunar surface. With that in mind, NASA gauged the likelihood for a similar space bullet striking a future moon base: about a one-in-10,000 chance per decade. “We’re probably safe going forward,” Heldmann said.
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯二号机组人员飞到了任何主要的年度流星体流之外，这意味着他们在不到一个小时内看到的五次撞击可能代表了小型陨石撞击月球表面的典型背景率。考虑到这一点，美国宇航局评估了类似的太空子弹击中未来月球基地的可能性：大约每十年一万分之一。 “我们未来可能会安全，”赫尔德曼说。

paras.en: The astronauts were also on the lookout for swarms of lunar dust. This jagged microscopic debris, easily dispersed by meteorite impacts and rocket exhaust, is corrosive, abrasive and adhesive. It makes quick work of wires, space suits and other hardware, chewing through them like space piranhas. Everyone hates it; it’s a major long-term hazard.
paras.zh: 宇航员也在寻找月球尘埃群。这种锯齿状的微观碎片很容易因陨石撞击和火箭尾气而分散，具有腐蚀性、磨蚀性和粘性。它可以快速处理电线、太空服和其他硬件，像太空食人鱼一样咀嚼它们。每个人都讨厌它；这是一个重大的长期危险。

paras.en: During the Apollo moon missions of the 1960s and 1970s, astronauts occasionally reported seeing hazes of sunlight-lofted dust drifting over parts of the lunar surface. But the Artemis II crew didn’t see any, suggesting that this strange phenomenon may be a transient problem rather than a persistent one.
paras.zh: 在 20 世纪 60 年代和 1970 年代的阿波罗登月任务期间，宇航员偶尔报告称看到阳光照射下的尘埃薄雾飘过月球表面的部分地区。但阿耳忒弥斯二号的船员没有看到任何现象，这表明这种奇怪的现象可能是一个暂时的问题，而不是一个持久的问题。

paras.en: The Artemis II images also revealed the subtle colors of lunar geology, showing that the moon’s seemingly monochrome surface is actually dappled with greens, yellows, grays and browns. Each of these hues, NASA’s analysis confirms, correspond to different types of ancient volcanism, from glasslike oozes to rubbly pyroclastic flow deposits. NASA also hoped that the crew could spy tectonic landforms during their flyby—things like faults, including those that could rupture and create prolonged, and potentially structure-toppling, moonquakes.
paras.zh: 阿耳忒弥斯二号的图像还揭示了月球地质的微妙色彩，表明月球看似单色的表面实际上布满了绿色、黄色、灰色和棕色的斑驳。美国宇航局的分析证实，这些颜色中的每一种都对应于不同类型的古代火山活动，从玻璃状软泥到碎石火山碎屑流沉积物。美国宇航局还希望机组人员能够在飞越期间监视构造地貌，例如断层，包括那些可能破裂并造成长期的、可能导致结构倒塌的月震。

paras.en: At one point, the crew caught a surreal series of arching crevasses in Oceanus Procellarum (the “Ocean of Storms,” a huge basin filled with primeval lava). These were wrinkle ridges, thought to form when the weight of the erupted lava squashes down on the moon’s crust, causing it to snap and contract. “The fact that they were able to see that from orbit was pretty phenomenal,” says Debra Needham, a member of the Artemis II science operations team.
paras.zh: 有一次，工作人员在 Oceanus Procellarum（“风暴之海”，一个充满原始熔岩的巨大盆地）中发现了一系列超现实的拱形裂缝。这些是皱纹脊，人们认为是当喷发的熔岩的重量压在月球地壳上，导致月球地壳破裂和收缩时形成的。 “他们能够从轨道上看到这一点，这一事实是相当惊人的，”阿耳忒弥斯二号科学操作团队的成员黛布拉·尼达姆说。

paras.en: Despite the fanfare of an official press conference, in truth, nothing in NASA’s report is especially revelatory. If anything, it serves as a reminder that unlocking the moon’s secrets—its alien geology, its hazardous landscapes and any scientific or economic treasures it may hold—relies getting a closer, surface-level look via more crewed and robotic investigations. In late September NASA also announced three new science payloads for near-future landings, all building on Artemis II’s success and adding to the case for an eventual moon base. One will monitor micrometeor impacts and other environmental threats at the lunar south pole, a second will search for hollow “lava tubes” that could be sites for underground habitats and a third will study how water ice might accumulate in and change the stability of lunar soil.
paras.zh: 尽管官方新闻发布会大张旗鼓，但事实上，美国宇航局的报告中没有什么特别具有启发性的内容。如果说有什么不同的话，那就是它提醒人们，解开月球的秘密——它的外星地质、危险的地貌以及它可能蕴藏的任何科学或经济宝藏——依赖于通过更多的载人和机器人调查来更近距离地观察月球表面。 9 月下旬，美国宇航局还宣布了三个用于近期着陆的新科学有效载荷，所有这些都建立在阿耳忒弥斯二号的成功基础上，并为最终月球基地的建立奠定了基础。其中一项将监测月球南极的微流星影响和其他环境威胁，第二项将寻找可能成为地下栖息地的中空“熔岩管”，第三项将研究水冰如何积聚并改变月球土壤的稳定性。

paras.en: The report’s emphasis on future exploration was also tempered by an intentional callback to the past. NASA officials noted that their report’s release date, October 7, has significance in spaceflight history: on this day, back in 1959, the Soviet Union’s Luna 3 space probe beamed back the first-ever images of the moon’s farside, showing it to be a heavily scarred, crater-filled wasteland.
paras.zh: 该报告对未来勘探的强调也因有意回顾过去而有所缓和。 NASA 官员指出，他们报告的发布日期 10 月 7 日在航天史上具有重要意义：1959 年的这一天，苏联的月球 3 号太空探测器传回了月球背面的第一张图像，显示月球背面是一片伤痕累累、布满陨石坑的荒地。

paras.en: Luna 3’s images were eye-opening but still blandly colorless and fuzzy—especially compared with the kaleidoscopic, panchromatic views from Artemis II’s lunar pirouette. The alluring vistas the astronauts captured on digital cameras and iPhones helped ensure that “the entire world was united around our mission, and our crew,” says Kelsey Young, Artemis II’s lunar science lead. If NASA sticks to its plan and voyages to the moon become commonplace, then extraordinary images like these will quickly become glorious in their ordinariness.
paras.zh: 月球 3 号的图像令人大开眼界，但仍然平淡无色且模糊，尤其是与阿耳忒弥斯二号月球旋转时的万花筒全色视图相比。阿耳忒弥斯二号月球科学负责人凯尔西·杨 (Kelsey Young) 表示，宇航员用数码相机和 iPhone 捕捉到的迷人景色有助于确保“整个世界团结在我们的使命和我们的机组人员周围”。如果美国宇航局坚持其计划，月球航行变得司空见惯，那么像这样的非凡图像很快就会在平凡中变得光彩夺目。

articles.title: This September was the hottest ever on record for the U.S.

paras.en: September 2026 shattered the record for the hottest September ever recorded in the contiguous U.S., according to new data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. It marks another sobering record for an already historically hot year.
paras.zh: 根据美国国家海洋和大气管理局的最新数据，2026 年 9 月打破了美国本土有记录以来最热 9 月的记录。这标志着本已历史炎热的一年又创下了一个发人深省的记录。

paras.en: This past January through September were the hottest first nine months of any year in the U.S. since at least 1895.
paras.zh: 今年一月到九月是美国至少自 1895 年以来每年最热的前九个月。

paras.en: Overall, the contiguous U.S. averaged a balmy 69.42 degrees Fahrenheit (20.79 degrees Celsius) in September—more than 4.5 degrees F (about 2.5 degrees C) higher than the historical 20th-century average.
paras.zh: 总体而言，美国本土 9 月平均气温为 69.42 华氏度（20.79 摄氏度），气候宜人，比 20 世纪的历史平均气温高出 4.5 华氏度（约 2.5 摄氏度）。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Whether 2026 will break the record for the U.S.’s hottest year—currently standing at 55.48 degrees F (about 13 degrees C), set in 2024—depends on the temperatures for October, November and December. As Scientific American previously reported, climate predictions are complicated. But what is clear is that such a warm September only makes the situation more dire.
paras.zh: 2026 年是否会打破美国最热年份的记录（目前为 2024 年创下的 55.48 华氏度（约 13 摄氏度））取决于 10 月、11 月和 12 月的气温。正如《科学美国人》之前报道的那样，气候预测很复杂。但显而易见的是，如此温暖的九月只会让情况变得更加可怕。

paras.en: Leading up to now, the period of the first eight months of the year, January–August, was exceptionally hot. If the period of September–December averages around 50.5 degrees F (10.3 degrees C)—a warm but not unusual scenario for recent years—the U.S. is likely to break its record, climatologist Zeke Hausfather previously told Scientific American.
paras.zh: 截至目前，今年前八个月，即一月至八月，天气异常炎热。气候学家 Zeke Hausfather 此前告诉《科学美国人》，如果 9 月至 12 月期间的平均气温约为 50.5 华氏度（10.3 摄氏度）左右（这是近年来的温暖但并不罕见的情况），美国可能会打破其记录。

paras.en: Crowning 2026 as the hottest year would only be part of the picture; climate change doesn’t care about records.
paras.zh: 将 2026 年定为最热的一年只是其中的一部分；气候变化并不关心记录。

paras.en: As Climate Central scientist Zachary Labe previously told Scientific American, “Whether 2026 ultimately ranks as number one or number three doesn’t distract from the bigger story that temperatures are rising across the country and leading to major impacts for communities.”
paras.zh: 正如气候中心科学家 Zachary Labe 此前告诉《科学美国人》的那样，“无论 2026 年最终排名第一还是第三，都不会分散人们对全国气温上升并对社区造成重大影响这一更大的故事的注意力。”

paras.en: Editor’s Note (10/8/26): This is a breaking news story and may be updated.
paras.zh: 编者注（10/8/26）：这是一个突发新闻报道，可能会更新。

articles.title: Gene therapy and special goggles give some blind people limited sight
articles.author: Nora Bradford

paras.en: Some blind people can now find a doorway or spot an object with the help of an experimental treatment and custom goggles.
paras.zh: 一些盲人现在可以借助实验治疗和定制护目镜找到门口或发现物体。

paras.en: Participants in a new study had blindness caused by a genetic disease called retinitis pigmentosa, which progressively kills off light-sensing cells in the retina. The treatment improved seven of 10 people’s light sensitivity, researchers report October 7 in New England Journal of Medicine. The findings build on a 2021 report that the same approach helped one blind man see and count objects.
paras.zh: 一项新研究的参与者因一种名为视网膜色素变性的遗传性疾病导致失明，这种疾病会逐渐杀死视网膜中的感光细胞。研究人员 10 月 7 日在《新英格兰医学杂志》上报告称，这种治疗改善了十分之七的人的光敏感度。这些发现建立在 2021 年的一份报告的基础上，该报告称同样的方法帮助一名盲人看到并计算物体。

paras.en: The treatment is based on optogenetics, a technique that uses genetic instructions to make cells respond to light. Rather than repair the retina’s damaged light detectors, it gives that ability to retinal ganglion cells that normally relay visual signals to the brain.
paras.zh: 该治疗基于光遗传学，这是一种利用遗传指令使细胞对光做出反应的技术。它不是修复视网膜受损的光探测器，而是赋予通常将视觉信号传递给大脑的视网膜神经节细胞这种能力。

paras.en: “This is a proof of concept that optogenetics can bring back some visual activity [and] object sensitivity,” says Botond Roska, neuroscientist at the Institute of Molecular and Clinical Ophthalmology Basel in Switzerland.
paras.zh: “这是光遗传学可以恢复一些视觉活动和物体敏感性的概念证明，”瑞士巴塞尔分子与临床眼科研究所的神经科学家 Botond Roska 说。

paras.en: Pioneering work on optogenetics snagged the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on October 5.
paras.zh: 光遗传学的开创性工作于 10 月 5 日荣获 2026 年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。

paras.en: Scientists have been experimenting with optogenetic therapies to rewire the eye and restore vision to people with degenerative eye diseases for more than a decade. Just as in the 2021 study, in the new work Roska and his colleagues injected genetic instructions for ChrimsonR, a light-sensitive protein derived from algae, into participants’ worse-seeing eye. The treatment made retinal ganglion cells in that eye sensitive to amber light. A camera in the custom goggles detected changes in brightness in what was in front of a study participant, and the goggles projected those changes onto the retina as pulses of amber light, activating the treated cells.
paras.zh: 十多年来，科学家们一直在试验光遗传学疗法，以重塑眼睛并恢复患有退行性眼病的人的视力。正如 2021 年的研究一样，Roska 和他的同事在新研究中将 ChrimsonR（一种源自藻类的光敏蛋白）的基因指令注入参与者视力较差的眼睛中。这种治疗使那只眼睛的视网膜神经节细胞对琥珀色的光敏感。定制护目镜中的摄像头检测到研究参与者面前的亮度变化，护目镜将这些变化以琥珀色光脉冲的形式投射到视网膜上，从而激活经过处理的细胞。

paras.en: Four of the eight study participants who completed behavioral testing after treatment were able to find a doorway or follow a line while wearing the goggles. No patient gained the ability to read visual words or see faces, but Roska and his colleagues hope to tackle that next.
paras.zh: 治疗后完成行为测试的八名研究参与者中有四人能够在戴着护目镜时找到门口或沿着路线走。没有患者获得阅读视觉文字或看到面孔的能力，但罗斯卡和他的同事希望下一步解决这个问题。

paras.en: But there’s a limitation to this work. The approach requires a working optic nerve to carry signals to the brain, says study coauthor José-Alain Sahel, an ophthalmologist at the University of Pittsburgh. It relies on cells in the retina communicating to the brain, so it cannot restore vision when that connection is damaged.
paras.zh: 但这项工作有一个局限性。该研究的合著者、匹兹堡大学眼科医生何塞·阿兰·萨赫尔 (José-Alain Sahel) 表示，这种方法需要有效的视神经将信号传递到大脑。它依赖于视网膜中的细胞与大脑进行通信，因此当该连接受损时，它无法恢复视力。

articles.title: An experimental drug kills fat cells, rather than shrinking them
articles.author: Tina Hesman Saey

paras.en: An experimental drug may melt away a dangerous type of fat that packs around internal organs.
paras.zh: 一种实验药物可能会融化内脏周围的一种危险脂肪。

paras.en: The drug, called CBL-514, specifically triggers fat cells to enter a death program called apoptosis. People who got injections of the experimental drug in their lower abdomens lost visceral fat, researchers reported October 1 at the annual meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes in Milan, Italy. Visceral fat sits deep in the abdomen where it chokes organs and can spur inflammation and health problems.
paras.zh: 这种药物名为 CBL-514，专门触发脂肪细胞进入称为细胞凋亡的死亡程序。研究人员 10 月 1 日在意大利米兰举行的欧洲糖尿病研究协会年会上报告称，在下腹部注射实验药物的人减少了内脏脂肪。内脏脂肪位于腹部深处，它会阻塞器官，并可能引发炎症和健康问题。

paras.en: Weight loss can shrink fat cells, but the cells are still there, poised to balloon up again.
paras.zh: 减肥可以缩小脂肪细胞，但细胞仍然存在，并准备再次膨胀。

paras.en: The team already knew the experimental drug could reduce subcutaneous fat, the pinchable fat that sits under the skin, in the abdomen. That surface fat doesn’t carry the same health risks that visceral fat does.
paras.zh: 研究小组已经知道这种实验药物可以减少皮下脂肪，即腹部皮下的可捏脂肪。表面脂肪不会带来与内脏脂肪相同的健康风险。

paras.en: In the new study, researchers examined MRIs from a subset of participants in two small clinical trials to track visceral fat levels. Study participants, who ranged from healthy weights to overweight, got injections of CBL-514 or placebo every three weeks for up to 12 weeks. The two groups started with about the same amount of visceral fat; 642.5 milliliters on average in the CBL-514 group and 677.4 milliliters in the placebo group. Four weeks after treatment, those who got the experimental drug had dropped almost 71 mL of visceral fat (a 12 percent decrease), while the placebo group gained 31 mL (a nearly 6 percent increase) of the dangerous fat in their abdomens.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，研究人员检查了两项小型临床试验中一部分参与者的核磁共振成像，以追踪内脏脂肪水平。研究参与者的体重范围从健康体重到超重，每三周注射一次 CBL-514 或安慰剂，持续长达 12 周。两组开始时的内脏脂肪量大致相同； CBL-514 组平均为 642.5 毫升，安慰剂组为 677.4 毫升。治疗 4 周后，服用实验药物的人减少了近 71 毫升的内脏脂肪（减少了 12%），而安慰剂组的腹部危险脂肪增加了 31 毫升（增加了近 6%）。

paras.en: Measurements taken at eight to 12 weeks after treatment showed the gap had widened. Those who got the experimental drug lost almost 63 mL — about a quarter cup — of visceral fat on average while the placebo group gained more than 78 mL of visceral fat over the starting point. Those results suggest that the drug might have health benefits by reducing visceral fat, which contributes to diabetes and heart problems. Larger clinical trials to test efficacy and safety of the drug are ongoing.
paras.zh: 治疗后 8 至 12 周进行的测量显示差距扩大了。那些服用实验药物的人平均减少了近 63 毫升（约四分之一杯）的内脏脂肪，而安慰剂组则比开始时增加了超过 78 毫升的内脏脂肪。这些结果表明，该药物可能通过减少内脏脂肪对健康有益，而内脏脂肪会导致糖尿病和心脏问题。更大规模的临床试验正在进行中，以测试该药物的功效和安全性。

articles.title: Kilauea’s display is revealing why volcanoes spew like a fountain show
articles.author: Carolyn Gramling

paras.en: Kilauea has been erupting almost continuously for nearly 200 years, and volcanologists have seen a lot of sides to Hawaii’s most active volcano. But in the last year, Kilauea started doing something new: firing up frequent fountains of lava.
paras.zh: 基拉韦厄火山近 200 年来几乎一直在喷发，火山学家已经看到了夏威夷最活跃火山的许多侧面。但去年，基拉韦厄开始做一些新的事情：频繁喷发熔岩喷泉。

paras.en: The volcano’s fountain era kicked off at dawn on December 23, 2024, with an eruption inside the summit crater of Halema’uma’u. Since then, Kilauea has put on a recurring pyrotechnic display of lava fountains, researchers report October 8 in Science. It produced 54 different lava fountains by September 2026, some of which shot as high as 457 meters into the sky.
paras.zh: 2024 年 12 月 23 日黎明，哈莱马乌马乌山顶火山口喷发，拉开了火山喷泉时代的序幕。研究人员于 10 月 8 日在《科学》杂志上报道称，从那时起，基拉韦厄火山就不断上演熔岩喷泉的烟火表演。到 2026 年 9 月，它产生了 54 个不同的熔岩喷泉，其中一些高达 457 米。

paras.en: During an eruption, which can last from hours to days, months or even years, occasional lava fountains aren’t unusual. But it’s rare to see repeated fountains — distinct bursts separated by minutes to weeks — during a single eruption. At Kilauea, these clustered spurts have only occurred three times since 1823, and never with such frequency.
paras.zh: 喷发可能持续数小时、数天、数月甚至数年，在喷发期间，偶尔出现熔岩喷泉并不罕见。但在单次喷发期间，很少看到重复的喷泉——间隔几分钟到几周的明显喷发。在基拉韦厄火山，自 1823 年以来，这种聚集性喷发只发生过 3 次，而且从未出现过如此频繁的情况。

paras.en: Thanks to their rarity, researchers have known relatively little about what initiates, sustains and ends these episodic fountains, say Ashton Flinders, a research geophysicist at the U.S. Geological Survey’s Hawaiian Volcano Observatory, based in Hilo, and colleagues. There have been two prevailing ideas: Water dissolved in magma — the underground, molten mix of rock and gas — rising from deep inside the volcano suddenly escapes as the pressure changes, leading to a burst of pyrotechnics; or a carbon dioxide–rich foam atop the trapped magma, like the pressurized froth over a shaken bottle of soda, suddenly and violently expands.
paras.zh: 美国地质调查局夏威夷火山观测站的研究地球物理学家阿什顿·弗林德斯 (Ashton Flinders) 及其同事表示，由于它们的稀有性，研究人员对这些间歇性喷泉的启动、维持和结束知之甚少。有两种流行的观点：溶解在岩浆中的水——地下岩石和气体的熔融混合物——随着压力的变化从火山深处升起，突然逸出，导致烟火爆发；或者被困岩浆顶部富含二氧化碳的泡沫，就像摇动的苏打水瓶上的加压泡沫一样，突然剧烈膨胀。

paras.en: Kilauea is the perfect laboratory in which to assess these hypotheses, the researchers say. It has been intensely studied by scientists and monitored by instruments for decades. Scientists continuously collect data on its seismic activity, temperature, low-frequency acoustics, how much the ground swells or deflates and the gases that escape. Using these data, researchers have begun to form a picture of what’s causing the relentless spewing.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，基拉韦厄火山是评估这些假设的完美实验室。数十年来，科学家们对其进行了深入研究并通过仪器对其进行了监测。科学家们不断收集有关其地震活动、温度、低频声学、地面膨胀或收缩程度以及逸出气体的数据。利用这些数据，研究人员已经开始了解导致不断喷涌的原因。

paras.en: Before each fountain, the team found, the floor of the bowl-shaped caldera would swell and tilt, suggesting magma was gathering beneath. As the eruption matured and the fountains continued, a pattern emerged, first appearing before the fourteenth fountain. Just before that eruption, the team detected a repetitive sequence of minutes-long bursts of seismic energy and low-frequency acoustics.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，在每个喷泉之前，碗状火山口的底部都会膨胀并倾斜，这表明岩浆正在聚集在下面。随着喷发的成熟和喷泉的持续，一种图案出现了，首先出现在第十四个喷泉之前。就在火山喷发之前，研究小组检测到了一系列重复的长达数分钟的地震能量爆发和低频声波。

paras.en: Those signals, the researchers say, are linked to the buildup and release of trapped gases in magma, which make it rise and fall through narrow volcanic vents in the rock like a piston in a car. The team also noted that while the volcano burped some sulfur dioxide gas, there was relatively little carbon dioxide, suggesting that the foam hypothesis wasn’t at work.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，这些信号与岩浆中滞留气体的积聚和释放有关，这使得岩浆像汽车中的活塞一样通过岩石中狭窄的火山喷口上升和下降。研究小组还指出，虽然火山喷出一些二氧化硫气体，但二氧化碳相对较少，这表明泡沫假说并不成立。

paras.en: This is just a preliminary glimpse into this phenomenon, and a lot of questions remain, Flinders and his colleagues say.
paras.zh: 弗林德斯和他的同事说，这只是对这一现象的初步了解，仍然存在很多问题。

articles.title: People With Dementia May Actually Live Longer if They Carry Extra Weight
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: Obesity in middle age is a significant risk factor for developing dementia in later life, but the relationship may be more complicated than we thought.
paras.zh: 中年肥胖是晚年患痴呆症的一个重要危险因素，但其中的关系可能比我们想象的更复杂。

paras.en: Researchers from the US and Canada have now turned up evidence that extra body weight is associated with a longer life once a dementia diagnosis has been given.
paras.zh: 美国和加拿大的研究人员现已发现证据表明，一旦诊断出痴呆症，体重增加与寿命延长有关。

paras.en: Considering how many health problems are linked to obesity – from high blood pressure to several cancers – it's a surprising finding.
paras.zh: 考虑到有多少健康问题与肥胖有关——从高血压到多种癌症——这是一个令人惊讶的发现。

paras.en: But the discovery may give experts some useful insight into how dementia develops and how it might be slowed down.
paras.zh: 但这一发现可能会让专家们了解痴呆症如何发展以及如何减缓其发展速度。

paras.en: The research team analyzed health records from 4,523 US adults aged 51 and over who didn't have dementia at the beginning of the study period but went on to develop it.
paras.zh: 研究小组分析了 4,523 名 51 岁及以上美国成年人的健康记录，这些人在研究开始时并未患有痴呆症，但后来却患上了痴呆症。

paras.en: Based on their body mass index (BMI) at the start, they were put into four groups: normal weight, overweight, class 1 obesity, and class 2/3 obesity.
paras.zh: 根据开始时的体重指数（BMI），将他们分为四组：正常体重、超重、1级肥胖和2/3级肥胖。

paras.en: As reported in the Journal of Alzheimer's Disease, over a follow-up period of up to 20 years, those who were at a normal weight were significantly more likely to die earlier.
paras.zh: 据《阿尔茨海默病杂志》报道，在长达 20 年的随访期内，体重正常的人更早死亡的可能性明显更高。

paras.en: "This doesn't mean that patients with dementia should attempt to become overweight or obese, as our study was not designed to test that question," says behavioral scientist Virginia Chang from the New York University School of Global Public Health.
paras.zh: 纽约大学全球公共卫生学院的行为科学家 Virginia Chang 表示：“这并不意味着痴呆症患者应该尝试变得超重或肥胖，因为我们的研究并不是为了测试这个问题。”

paras.en: "But our findings do suggest that weight status may serve as a useful prognostic signal for survival at the time of dementia diagnosis. They also support the notion that nutrition is a key factor in the health and survival of people with dementia."
paras.zh: “但我们的研究结果确实表明，体重状况可以作为痴呆症诊断时生存的有用预后信号。它们还支持这样的观点，即营养是痴呆症患者健康和生存的关键因素。”

paras.en: Compared to people of normal weight, the overweight group had a 16 percent lower risk of death over the study period.
paras.zh: 与正常体重的人相比，超重组在研究期间的死亡风险降低了 16%。

paras.en: For those with class 1 obesity it was 27 percent lower, and for those with class 2/3 obesity it was a 22 percent lower risk.
paras.zh: 对于 1 级肥胖者，风险降低 27%；对于 2/3 级肥胖者，风险降低 22%。

paras.en: That was after the researchers factored in other important influences on mortality rate, including sex, educational level, race and ethnicity, smoking status, and other chronic health conditions.
paras.zh: 研究人员考虑了对死亡率的其他重要影响因素，包括性别、教育水平、种族和民族、吸烟状况以及其他慢性健康状况。

paras.en: The researchers actively checked for any bias that might have crept in. For example, they looked at the weight history of the participants to see if those in the normal weight bracket might have previously been overweight and lost weight due to ill health, making them more vulnerable – but the associations still held.
paras.zh: 研究人员积极检查是否存在任何可能潜入的偏见。例如，他们查看了参与者的体重历史，看看正常体重范围内的人之前是否可能因健康状况不佳而超重和体重减轻，从而使他们更容易受到伤害——但这种关联仍然存在。

paras.en: "Because this finding is somewhat counterintuitive, an important question is whether it could simply be an artifact of bias," says gerontologist Yuan Zhang from the Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚大学梅尔曼公共卫生学院的老年学家张远说：“因为这一发现有些违反直觉，所以一个重要的问题是它是否可能只是偏见的产物。”

paras.en: "Our analyses suggest that the major sources of bias we examined do not explain the survival advantage associated with higher weight."
paras.zh: “我们的分析表明，我们检查的主要偏差来源并不能解释与较高体重相关的生存优势。”

paras.en: The next question is why this counterintuitive connection exists.
paras.zh: 下一个问题是为什么存在这种违反直觉的联系。

paras.en: For now, it's not clear, but the researchers speculate that dementia may lead to people skipping meals and forgetting to eat. For those who have more body fat or muscle in reserve, that's potentially less of an issue.
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚，但研究人员推测痴呆症可能会导致人们不吃饭和忘记吃饭。对于那些体内有更多脂肪或肌肉储备的人来说，这可能不是什么问题。

paras.en: "Nutrition can be a big problem for people with dementia," says Chang.
paras.zh: “对于痴呆症患者来说，营养可能是一个大问题，”张说。

paras.en: "They may experience wasting and an inability to eat, which can be due to changes in the brain's central drive, leading to loss of appetite and initiative, increased energy expenditure, and difficulties feeding themselves."
paras.zh: “他们可能会出现消瘦和无法进食的情况，这可能是由于大脑中枢驱动力的变化导致的，导致食欲和主动性丧失，能量消耗增加以及进食困难。”

paras.en: This isn't a completely new idea. The same 'obesity paradox has been seen in heart and kidney disease as well.
paras.zh: 这并不是一个全新的想法。同样的“肥胖悖论”也出现在心脏和肾脏疾病中。

paras.en: Further research will be needed, specifically tracking weight and eating habits over time, to understand why the association is there.
paras.zh: 还需要进一步的研究，特别是随着时间的推移跟踪体重和饮食习惯，以了解为什么存在这种关联。

paras.en: For now, it's not evidence of direct cause and effect, so it's not certain that weight is what's keeping people alive for longer. However, there's a strong case that obesity status is a signal worth paying attention to for people with dementia.
paras.zh: 目前，这还不是直接因果关系的证据，因此还不能确定体重是否能让人们活得更久。然而，有充分的证据表明，对于痴呆症患者来说，肥胖状况是一个值得关注的信号。

paras.en: "While the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood, these findings suggest that weight status at diagnosis may serve as a useful prognostic indicator alongside other factors," the researchers explain.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说：“虽然潜在的机制尚未完全了解，但这些发现表明，诊断时的体重状况可能与其他因素一起作为有用的预后指标。”

paras.en: The research has been published in The Journal of Alzheimer's Disease.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《阿尔茨海默病杂志》上。

articles.title: Scientists Collected Deep-Sea Rocks. They Spontaneously Caught Fire in The Lab.
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Scientists investigating the possibility of a 'gold rush' on the bottom of the ocean have hit upon an unforeseen 'landmine'.
paras.zh: 科学家们在调查海底“淘金热”的可能性时发现了一个无法预见的“地雷”。

paras.en: Researchers at the United States Geological Survey (USGS) are now warning that some deep-sea minerals may spontaneously combust when they are brought to the surface.
paras.zh: 美国地质调查局（USGS）的研究人员现在警告说，一些深海矿物在被带到海面时可能会自燃。

paras.en: In 2022, that happened to two samples of metal-sulfide rocks collected from the deep seafloor.
paras.zh: 2022 年，从深海底采集的两份金属硫化物岩石样本就发生了这种情况。

paras.en: The event caused temperatures above 100 °C in the lab and completely oxidized the original samples.
paras.zh: 该事件导致实验室温度超过 100 °C，原始样品被完全氧化。

paras.en: An article on the discovery, published in Scientific Reports, is being shared early, before full editing, to give the public faster access to new research.
paras.zh: 《科学报告》上发表的一篇有关这一发现的文章在全面编辑之前就已提前分享，以便公众更快地获得新研究成果。

paras.en: According to the USGS, this is a "potential hazard that could merit special consideration if deep-sea mining of seafloor massive sulfide deposits moves forward".
paras.zh: 美国地质勘探局表示，“如果海底块状硫化物矿床的深海开采继续进行，这是一个值得特别考虑的潜在危险”。

paras.en: "The production of heat through exothermic reactions has not been investigated in seafloor massive sulfide deposits but has the potential to cause rapid onset fires on ships," claims the recent article.
paras.zh: 最近的文章声称：“尚未在海底大量硫化物沉积物中研究通过放热反应产生的热量，但有可能导致船舶快速起火。”

paras.en: The combustible rocks were collected by the USGS in 2022, during a deep-sea investigation of the Escanaba Trough, in collaboration with the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
paras.zh: 这些可燃岩石是美国地质勘探局 (USGS) 于 2022 年与海洋能源管理局 (BOEM) 和美国国家海洋和大气管理局 (NOAA) 合作对埃斯卡纳巴海槽进行深海调查时收集的。

paras.en: The Escanaba Trough sits in the US Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) off the Oregon–California border, where hydrothermal activity has created deep-sea deposits rich in metals such as copper, zinc, and iron.
paras.zh: 埃斯卡纳巴海槽位于俄勒冈州和加利福尼亚州边境附近的美国专属经济区 (EEZ)，这里的热液活动创造了富含铜、锌和铁等金属的深海矿藏。

paras.en: Using a remotely operated vehicle, researchers collected 57 hydrothermal rock samples from four regions in the trough.
paras.zh: 研究人员使用遥控车辆从海槽的四个区域收集了 57 个热液岩石样本。

paras.en: Most of these samples contained metal sulfides as a major mineral.
paras.zh: 这些样品中的大多数含有金属硫化物作为主要矿物。

paras.en: When researchers freeze-dried and crushed them in the laboratory, however, two of the samples spontaneously combusted.
paras.zh: 然而，当研究人员在实验室中将它们冷冻干燥并粉碎时，其中两个样品自燃了。

paras.en: The discovery that some rocks from the deep may catch fire on land comes at an important time.
paras.zh: 一些来自深处的岩石可能会在陆地上着火的发现来得正是时候。

paras.en: The International Seabed Authority (ISA) has granted exploration contracts for sulfide minerals on two deep-sea ridges, the Northern Mid-Atlantic Ridge and Southwest Indian Ridge.
paras.zh: 国际海底管理局（ISA）已授予两个深海海脊（北大西洋中脊和西南印度海脊）硫化物矿物的勘探合同。

paras.en: Mining has not yet taken place, but when it does, there is reason to tread cautiously.
paras.zh: 采矿业尚未发生，但一旦发生，就有理由谨慎行事。

paras.en: Sulfide minerals are special because they can contain precious metals, like gold, silver, copper, or zinc.
paras.zh: 硫化物矿物很特殊，因为它们含有贵金属，如金、银、铜或锌。

paras.en: But they can also spontaneously combust.
paras.zh: 但它们也可以自燃。

paras.en: Heavy sedimentation in the deep ocean, for instance, can promote the formation of hydrothermally derived petroleum.
paras.zh: 例如，深海的严重沉积可以促进热液衍生石油的形成。

paras.en: This material can then be hidden within metal sulfide minerals, and on land, it has the ability to self-heat.
paras.zh: 这种材料可以隐藏在金属硫化物矿物中，在陆地上，它具有自热能力。

paras.en: "The new research suggests that some seafloor massive sulfide rocks have physical and chemical properties that could make them behave very differently from comparable mineral deposits mined on land," warns a press release from the USGS.
paras.zh: 美国地质勘探局的一份新闻稿警告说：“新的研究表明，一些海底块状硫化物岩石的物理和化学特性可能使它们的行为与陆地上开采的同类矿藏截然不同。”

paras.en: To figure out what sets these combustible rocks apart, researchers compared the mineralogy, chemical composition, and thermal behavior of the samples they collected in 2022.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚这些可燃岩石的独特之处，研究人员比较了他们在 2022 年收集的样本的矿物学、化学成分和热行为。

paras.en: Tar and petroleum didn't seem to be the problem. Instead, researchers found that the self-combusting rocks were made mostly of nanocrystalline marcasite.
paras.zh: 焦油和石油似乎不是问题。相反，研究人员发现自燃岩石主要由纳米晶白铁矿组成。

paras.en: This is a form of iron sulfide that appears to be especially unstable in the presence of oxygen.
paras.zh: 这是硫化铁的一种形式，在氧气存在下似乎特别不稳定。

paras.en: The addition of heat and mechanochemical forces, like crushing, breaking, and grinding, can supply energy to initiate oxidation.
paras.zh: 热量和机械化学力的增加，如压碎、破碎和研磨，可以提供能量来引发氧化。

paras.en: When this sample oxidizes, it can lead to self-heating.
paras.zh: 当该样品氧化时，会导致自热。

paras.en: This doesn't mean every rock on the ocean floor containing marcasite is a hazard, but it is a potential danger that could help shape safety regulations for a new industry.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着海底每块含有白铁矿的岩石都是危险的，但它是一种潜在的危险，可以帮助制定新行业的安全法规。

paras.en: "If seafloor massive sulfide mining occurs, rocks brought to the surface would experience conditions dramatically different from those on the seafloor, including exposure to oxygen and changes in temperature, pressure, and moisture," the USGS explains.
paras.zh: 美国地质调查局解释说：“如果进行海底大量硫化物开采，浮出水面的岩石将经历与海底截然不同的条件，包括暴露在氧气中以及温度、压力和湿度的变化。”

paras.en: "Such changes could affect how sulfide minerals react and how much heat they generate."
paras.zh: “这些变化可能会影响硫化物矿物的反应方式以及它们产生的热量。”

paras.en: Deep-sea mining comes with many warnings, not just for the safety of humans.
paras.zh: 深海采矿伴随着许多警告，不仅仅是为了人类的安全。

paras.en: Many environmentalists are concerned that this burgeoning new industry may be the last straw for precious ocean ecosystems, already at risk.
paras.zh: 许多环保人士担心，这一新兴产业可能成为压垮已经处于危险之中的珍贵海洋生态系统的最后一根稻草。

paras.en: The consequences, if we are not careful, could blow up in our faces.
paras.zh: 如果我们不小心的话，后果可能会在我们脸上爆炸。

paras.en: The research has been published in Scientific Reports.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学报告》上。

articles.title: Scientists Find Squid Are Covered in Hair-Like Cells Remarkably Similar to The Ones in Human Ears
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: The skin of a squid, surprisingly, has much in common with an organ inside your ear.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，鱿鱼的皮肤与耳朵内的器官有很多相似之处。

paras.en: As reported in a new study in Current Biology, scientists have found that squid are covered in cells with little hair-like structures, similar to those inside human ears, which detect information carried by passing waves.
paras.zh: 《当代生物学》的一项新研究报告称，科学家发现乌贼的细胞表面覆盖着细小的毛发状结构，类似于人耳内部的细胞，可以检测通过的波携带的信息。

paras.en: For humans, these little hairs help us to interpret sound waves from a melody or a voice, or the honk of an impatient driver.
paras.zh: 对于人类来说，这些小毛发帮助我们解读旋律、声音或不耐烦的司机的喇叭声中的声波。

paras.en: For squid, it's all the little details carried in water movement: the twitch of nearby prey, the rumble of a distant shore, the pull of a current.
paras.zh: 对于鱿鱼来说，它是水运动中的所有小细节：附近猎物的抽搐、远处海岸的隆隆声、水流的拉力。

paras.en: Until now, scientists had no idea that squid were totally studded with these hair cells – and the discovery may be able to tell us something about our own hearing equipment.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，科学家们还不知道乌贼身上完全布满了这些毛细胞——这一发现也许能够告诉我们一些关于我们自己的听力设备的信息。

paras.en: Brian McDermott from Case Western Reserve University is an otolaryngologist – a scientist who studies inner ears, noses, and throats.
paras.zh: 凯斯西储大学的布莱恩·麦克德莫特 (Brian McDermott) 是一位耳鼻喉科医生，是一位研究内耳、鼻子和喉咙的科学家。

paras.en: As a medical researcher, he started out trying to understand human hearing and deafness. But by tracing the lineage of the specialized hair cells that bring music to our ears, he has now arrived at the longfin inshore squid (Doryteuthis pealeii): an animal separated from humans by hundreds of millions of years of evolution.
paras.zh: 作为一名医学研究员，他开始尝试了解人类的听力和耳聋。但通过追踪将音乐传到我们耳朵的特殊毛细胞的谱系，他现在找到了长鳍近海乌贼（Doryteuthis pealeii）：一种经过数亿年进化与人类分离的动物。

paras.en: "Squid are cephalopods with a diverse population of hair cells on the surface of their bodies, which may yield insights not only into how these fascinating animals detect water movement to survive, but also into how hearing and deafness occur in humans," McDermott says.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特说：“鱿鱼是头足类动物，其身体表面有多种毛细胞，这不仅可以帮助我们了解这些迷人的动物如何检测水的运动以求生存，还可以了解人类的听力和耳聋是如何发生的。”

paras.en: Before we go further, it's probably important to note that the hair cells we're talking about here have nothing to do with the hair that grows from follicles in your skin. In all vertebrates, except fish, hair cells exist only within organs in our ears (remember the fish part – we'll come back to that).
paras.zh: 在我们进一步讨论之前，可能需要注意的是，我们在这里讨论的毛细胞与皮肤毛囊长出的毛发无关。在所有脊椎动物中，除了鱼之外，毛细胞只存在于我们耳朵的器官内（记住鱼的部分——我们稍后会讨论这一点）。

paras.en: For vertebrates that live on land, hair cells are crucial to hearing. They line the inner surface of the cochlea, which is a spiral-shaped, fluid-filled organ that, from the outside, looks a lot like a snail.
paras.zh: 对于生活在陆地上的脊椎动物来说，毛细胞对于听力至关重要。它们排列在耳蜗的内表面，耳蜗是一个螺旋形的、充满液体的器官，从外面看起来很像蜗牛。

paras.en: If someone hears a sound, it's typically because waves in the air have traveled into their ears, vibrating their eardrums and a succession of tiny bones that then translate this movement into waves in the cochlear fluid.
paras.zh: 如果有人听到声音，通常是因为空气中的波进入了他们的耳朵，振动了他们的耳膜和一系列微小的骨头，然后将这种运动转化为耳蜗液中的波。

paras.en: It's these fluid waves that the hair cells of a human ear are attuned to. As the 'hairs' wave about within the cochlear fluid, their movement is translated by the cell into a message that can be sent on to the brain. It's at this point that we perceive sound.
paras.zh: 人耳的毛细胞正是适应这些流体波。当“毛发”在耳蜗液内摆动时，它们的运动被细胞转化为可以发送到大脑的信息。正是在这一点上，我们感知到了声音。

paras.en: Inside a human ear, not all hair cells are identical. Some have bundles of long hairs, which are much better at picking up low-pitched sounds, while some have short hairs, ideal for high-pitched frequencies.
paras.zh: 在人耳内部，并非所有毛细胞都是相同的。有些有长毛束，更适合拾取低音调的声音，而有些则有短毛，非常适合拾取高音调的声音。

paras.en: Here's where fish come in. Fish, unlike many other vertebrates, have hair cells on the outside of their bodies, in an organ called the lateral line.
paras.zh: 这就是鱼的用武之地。与许多其他脊椎动物不同，鱼在身体外部的称为侧线的器官中具有毛细胞。

paras.en: Other sea creatures – including squid – have lateral lines too. When you spend your whole life underwater, the waves in your surroundings are already transmitted by fluid.
paras.zh: 其他海洋生物——包括鱿鱼——也有侧线。当你一生都在水下度过时，你周围的波浪已经通过流体传播了。

paras.en: Unlike us landlubbers, marine animals don't have to translate the waves from air to fluid: their hair cells can pick up that motion directly from the source.
paras.zh: 与我们旱鸭子不同的是，海洋动物不需要将波浪从空气转化为液体：它们的毛细胞可以直接从源头接收到这种运动。

paras.en: But in fish, the 'hairs' are more or less the same length.
paras.zh: 但鱼类的“毛发”长度大致相同。

paras.en: Squids, on the other hand, seem to have evolved diverse, specialized hair cells much like our own.
paras.zh: 另一方面，鱿鱼似乎进化出了多种、专门的毛细胞，就像我们自己的毛细胞一样。

paras.en: He and his team mapped the entire bodies of several hatchling squid using light-sheet microscopy, which makes the squids' hair cells light up in pictures.
paras.zh: 他和他的团队使用光片显微镜绘制了几只刚孵化的乌贼的整个身体，这使得乌贼的毛细胞在照片中发光。

paras.en: "Unexpectedly, we identified hair bundles organized in two patterns: previously
paras.zh: “出乎意料的是，我们发现了以两种模式组织的发束：以前

paras.en: described linear arrays and broad regional fields that have not been explicitly reported in squid or fish, which we term lateral line fields," the team reports.
paras.zh: 描述了线性阵列和广泛的区域场，这些区域在鱿鱼或鱼类中尚未明确报道，我们称之为侧线场，”该团队报告道。

paras.en: "Anatomical positions and corresponding variation in hair bundle lengths suggest some lateral lines detect distinct stimuli."
paras.zh: “解剖位置和发束长度的相应变化表明一些侧线检测到不同的刺激。”

paras.en: For instance, on the squid's mantle, hair bundles were very short compared to those on the head lateral line.
paras.zh: 例如，与头部侧线上的毛束相比，乌贼外套膜上的毛束非常短。

paras.en: "Our results show that the whole squid's surface is elaborately ornamented with varied lateral lines that likely register specific types of local water movements," the team concludes.
paras.zh: 研究小组总结道：“我们的结果表明，整个鱿鱼的表面都精心装饰着不同的侧线，这些侧线可能记录了当地特定类型的水运动。”

paras.en: It's pretty fascinating stuff in its own right, but McDermott's interests are primarily medical. He believes squid could be useful models for understanding how human hearing works, or, in some cases, doesn't.
paras.zh: 这本身就是一件非常有趣的事情，但麦克德莫特的兴趣主要是医学。他认为鱿鱼可能是了解人类听力如何工作的有用模型，或者在某些情况下却不能。

paras.en: "Often, when a child is born deaf or a hearing person loses their hearing, it is the hair bundle that has been damaged," McDermott said.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特说：“通常，当孩子出生时耳聋或听力正常的人失去听力时，受损的是发束。”

paras.en: "So, studying the squid's hair bundle holds promise for understanding how hearing loss occurs."
paras.zh: “因此，研究鱿鱼的毛束有望了解听力损失是如何发生的。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Current Biology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《当代生物学》上。

articles.title: Scientists build a nuclear clock that could make atomic clocks obsolete

paras.en: Scientists build a nuclear clock that could make atomic clocks obsolete
paras.zh: 科学家建造了一种核钟，可以使原子钟过时

paras.en: Researchers in Vienna have built the worldâs first self-stabilizing nuclear clock, bringing scientists closer to a new era of ultra-precise timekeeping.
paras.zh: 维也纳的研究人员建造了世界上第一个自稳定核钟，使科学家们更接近超精确计时的新时代。

paras.en: - Scientists in Vienna have achieved a major breakthrough in timekeeping by creating the worldâs first self-stabilizing nuclear clock, a technology that could eventually surpass even the most precise atomic clocks. Instead of relying on electrons in atoms, the clock uses the tiny nuclei of thorium atoms, which are far less sensitive to outside disturbances.
paras.zh: - 维也纳的科学家创造了世界上第一个自稳定核钟，在计时方面取得了重大突破，这项技术最终可能超越最精确的原子钟。该时钟不依赖原子中的电子，而是使用钍原子的微小原子核，钍原子核对外界干扰的敏感度要低得多。

paras.en: Scientists have reached a major milestone in the quest to build an entirely new kind of clock. After decades of research, a team in Vienna has developed the world's first self-stabilizing nuclear clock, a device that could eventually measure time with far greater precision than today's most advanced atomic clocks.
paras.zh: 科学家们在建造一种全新时钟的探索中达到了一个重要的里程碑。经过数十年的研究，维也纳的一个团队开发出了世界上第一个自稳定核钟，这种装置最终可以比当今最先进的原子钟更精确地测量时间。

paras.en: Unlike earlier prototypes, the new nuclear clock can maintain its own stability without depending on a conventional atomic clock. Researchers have demonstrated that it can operate steadily for more than 24 hours without intervention.
paras.zh: 与早期的原型不同，新型核钟可以在不依赖传统原子钟的情况下保持自身的稳定性。研究人员证明，它可以在无需干预的情况下稳定运行超过24小时。

paras.en: The achievement represents an important advance in precision measurement, also known as metrology. By using atomic nuclei as exceptionally stable references, nuclear clocks could eventually allow scientists to measure time and other physical quantities with levels of accuracy that existing technologies cannot reach.
paras.zh: 这一成就代表了精密测量（也称为计量学）的重要进步。通过使用原子核作为异常稳定的参考，核钟最终可以让科学家以现有技术无法达到的精度水平测量时间和其他物理量。

paras.en: Why Thorium Holds the Key to Nuclear Clocks
paras.zh: 为什么钍是核钟的关键

paras.en: The breakthrough relies on an unusual property of thorium atomic nuclei that scientists have investigated for decades.
paras.zh: 这一突破依赖于钍原子核的一种不寻常的特性，科学家们已经研究了几十年。

paras.en: Atomic nuclei can exist in different energy states, but moving between those states typically requires enormous amounts of energy. Thorium is a rare exception. Two of its nuclear energy states are separated by an unusually small energy gap, making it possible to trigger a transition between them using laser light.
paras.zh: 原子核可以以不同的能量状态存在，但在这些状态之间移动通常需要大量的能量。钍是一个罕见的例外。它的两个核能态被异常小的能隙隔开，使得利用激光触发它们之间的转变成为可能。

paras.en: This property is crucial because it allows researchers to control the energy state of a nucleus with a laser, something that is not possible in the same way for most other atomic nuclei. Scientists can then use this extremely precise transition as a reference for measuring time.
paras.zh: 这一特性至关重要，因为它使研究人员能够用激光控制原子核的能量状态，而这对于大多数其他原子核来说是不可能的。然后，科学家可以使用这种极其精确的转变作为测量时间的参考。

paras.en: A major breakthrough came in April 2024, when researchers led by Prof. Thorsten Schumm at the Institute of Atomic and Subatomic Physics at TU Wien, working with a team led by Prof. Ekkehard Peik at PTB Braunschweig, identified the long-sought nuclear transition experimentally. They demonstrated for the first time that laser beams could excite thorium nuclei.
paras.zh: 2024 年 4 月，一项重大突破出现，由维也纳工业大学原子和亚原子物理研究所的 Thorsten Schumm 教授领导的研究人员与 PTB Braunschweig 的 Ekkehard Peik 教授领导的团队合作，通过实验确定了人们长期寻求的核跃迁。他们首次证明激光束可以激发钍原子核。

paras.en: Further progress followed in the fall of 2024. The researchers connected their thorium excitation apparatus to a conventional optical atomic clock, demonstrating that the nuclei could serve as a highly precise timekeeping reference.
paras.zh: 2024 年秋天取得了进一步的进展。研究人员将他们的钍激发装置连接到传统的光学原子钟，证明原子核可以作为高精度的计时参考。

paras.en: Although this established the basic principle of a nuclear clock, one essential capability was still missing: the ability to maintain its own accuracy independently.
paras.zh: 虽然这确立了核钟的基本原理，但仍然缺少一项基本能力：独立保持自身精度的能力。

paras.en: Scientists Build a Nuclear Clock That Stabilizes Itself
